plant.description: A water reservoir. Input u in [0,1] is pump duty and raises the level; the reservoir drains on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a noisy level reading.

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Magnitude of DC gain and response lag plus noise level at a mid input; needed to map target level to pump range and to set safe controller speed without oscillation.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with modest lag is correct, y will start rising from ~0.34 within 1-2 s at roughly 0.01-0.03 per s toward ~0.45-0.55, with small noisy ripple, and will not reach steady state in 10 s if time constant is several seconds.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: High-input DC gain and steady-state u needed to hold 0.6; E1 suggests u=0.5 equilibrates near 0.30, so a second amplitude near the top discriminates linearity and target feasibility for control sizing.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain holds, y should stop falling and rise from ~0.33 within 1-2 s at ~0.01-0.04 per s to ~0.38-0.48 by 5 s with ~+/-0.015 noise; if y stays flat near 0.32-0.34, high-end gain is very low and holding 0.6 may be infeasible.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Drain behavior at u=0 and drain time constant, discriminating holding vs decaying level and allowing estimate of u needed to hold 0.6 for control design.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with drainage is correct, y will decay promptly from ~0.46 with no rise, initial slope about -0.02 to -0.06 per s, reaching ~0.20-0.35 after 10 s with +/-0.015 noise; if y holds flat near 0.46, drainage is negligible.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: High-mid DC gain and time constant to estimate u needed to hold 0.6 and set controller gain/speed; discriminates linear K~0.6 vs saturating/low high-end gain.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive linear gain with tau ~8-12s is right, y will rise promptly from ~0.23 with initial slope ~0.02-0.035 per s to ~0.35-0.45 by 8 s with +/-0.02 noise, still rising at end; if y stalls near 0.25-0.30, high-end gain is much lower and holding 0.6 is infeasible.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state u needed to hold 0.6 and high-end linearity; discriminates linear K~0.8-0.9 needing u~0.7 vs low high-end gain needing u~1.0, which sets controller feedforward and gain to reach target without oscillation.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with tau ~8-12s holds, y will stay flat for ~1-2s lag then rise from ~0.36 at ~0.02-0.035 per s to ~0.46-0.52 by 5s, still rising, with +/-0.015 noise; if high-end gain saturates, y will stall near 0.38-0.42.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state u needed to hold 0.6 and high-end linearity near target; discriminates u~0.7 vs u~0.9 to set feedforward and controller gain without overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with tau ~10-15s holds, y will rise promptly from ~0.48 at ~0.02-0.03 per s to ~0.56-0.60 by 4 s, still rising, with +/-0.02 noise; if high-end gain saturates, y will stall near 0.50-0.53.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Pure delay length, which discriminates slower-response from weaker-actuator/faster-outflow/sensor and sets safe controller speed.
experiments.expected_observation: If increased pure delay ~10-14s is correct, y will stay near 0.07 for a few seconds then rise due to the prior 0.85 in transit starting ~12-14s after 205.2 to ~0.3-0.5 at ~0.02-0.04 per s, then fall after the delay of this 0 command elapses; if delay were still 1-3s, rise would have already occurred and y would stay low/fall.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Pure delay length from a clean zero pipeline, which discriminates long-delay from weaker-actuator/faster-outflow/sensor and sets safe controller speed and prediction horizon.
experiments.expected_observation: If increased pure delay ~18-24s is correct, y will stay flat near 0.10-0.15 with only +/-0.02 noise for the full 14 s with no sustained rise, because the step issued at ~257.3 is still in transit; if delay were still 1-3s, y would start rising within 2-3 s at ~0.02 per s to ~0.25-0.35 by 14 s.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Exact pure-delay length from a clean zero pipeline, which discriminates long-delay from other changes and sets controller prediction horizon and safe speed.
experiments.expected_observation: If long pure delay ~18-24s is correct, y will stay near 0.0-0.05 for ~6-10 s more (14s already elapsed since 0.5 issued at 257.3), then rise at ~0.02-0.04 per s to ~0.2-0.4 by end; if delay were short, rise would have already occurred in E8.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain and approach rate at u=0.5 under long delay, which sets feedforward u to hold 0.6 and safe controller speed and prediction horizon.
experiments.expected_observation: If long pure delay ~24-25s with unchanged gain/tau is correct, y will continue rising from ~0.13 at ~0.015-0.03 per s to ~0.3-0.45 by end, still rising, with +/-0.02 noise; if actuator weaker, y will stall near 0.15-0.20; if outflow faster, y will flatten low.

ledger.statement: Increasing pump duty u raises the steady-state level y (positive DC gain).
At u=0 the level decays on its own due to drainage rather than holding constant.
There is no large dead-zone; even u ~0.5 produces a measurable rise versus u=0, but u~0.1-0.2 is untested.
Response shows short pure delay ~1-3 s and dominant first-order lag with time constant ~8-15 s.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear with K~0.8-1.1 across u=0.5-0.9 so mid-level steps predict high-end gain within ~30%.
Holding y=0.6 at steady state requires high-moderate pump u~0.65-0.78.
Sensor noise is small (std <0.02) relative to the 0.10 control band so second-scale averaging reveals true level.
Change is slower response, specifically pure delay increased from ~1-2s to ~24-25s, causing overshoot and oscillation.
Change is weaker actuator: same u produces smaller rise rate and lower held level.
Change is faster outflow: faster fall at u=0 and lower level held by same u.
Change is sensor offset or noise increase, not plant dynamics.
